headline: The jersey says Cleveland. The street says The Land.
thesis: Cleveland is two markets: a 216 split by the Cuyahoga into East Side and West Side, and an Akron 330 that claims the basketball origin story. Its fans believe only what they've watched happen, from The Drive, The Fumble and The Shot to the 2016 Game 7. The 2026-27 City Edition revives the 2018-19 Earned design with a plain 'Cleveland' wordmark. As the first in five City Editions not to say 'The Land', it hands the community's nickname back to the street. First, launch in two layers: Nike 'Cleveland' pieces on the City Edition on-sale, plus a licensed 'The Land' side line led by a paid Black Cleveland designer. Second, build a Karamu House-led program for the noon MLK Day game against Detroit, the marquee home date in a season with no opening-night or Christmas Day game. The rest is print and embroidery on existing blanks: Ore Dock winter layers, the 330 capsule, a player-free LeBron gratitude night and a Playoff Tour that prints only what happened.

archetype.name: The 3-1 Believer
archetype.description: This fan keeps score in Cleveland scars: The Drive, The Fumble, The Shot. There's one release, the 2016 comeback from 3-1 down that ended a 52-year drought in a Game 7. They still call the arena the Q. Last spring's 125-94 Game 7 rout of No. 1 Detroit was fun for exactly one series, until the Knicks sweep. So they buy what has happened, not what's promised, and say 216 or 330 before any slogan.

pulse.teamMoment: Cleveland went 52-30, won two Game 7s (one a 125-94 rout of No. 1 Detroit) and got swept in the East Finals by the eventual champion Knicks. Then it went all in: Mitchell extended, Harden re-signed and the last tradable first spent on Peyton Watson. It's title or bust, with no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Optimistic and impatient. The playoff run made believers, but the Knicks sweep, thinner depth (Wade, Ellis and Nance are gone) and a scout's public doubt keep title talk guarded.

topInsights.title: The nickname is off the jersey and back on the street
topInsights.insight: The 2026-27 City Edition is the first in five to say 'Cleveland' instead of 'The Land', and every lens reads the gap the same way. 'The Land' is community vocabulary, rooted in Black Cleveland and hip-hop and worn on bar walls, murals and homegrown tees. Leaving it to the street is an opening, but only if the street leads and earns from it.
topInsights.implication: Launch in two layers. Nike makes 'Cleveland' wordmark pieces that follow the City Edition on-sale. A licensed 'The Land' / 216 side line gets a named, paid Black Cleveland lead, with the revenue and credit sitting with local partners. Never frame it as a correction.

topInsights.title: 216 and 330 are two markets, with Nike's own door between them
topInsights.insight: Akron sees itself as the origin of Cleveland hoops, not a suburb: St. Vincent-St. Mary, I Promise, Devo, the Black Keys, Rubber City tire heritage. Between the two metros, the Nike Factory Store at Aurora Premium Outlets (formerly Aurora Farms) catches both.
topInsights.implication: Build a separate 330 capsule as print and embellishment on existing blanks: generic tread texture, stripe-and-numeral graphics, wine and tread black. Sell it at Aurora and Summit Mall instead of folding it into a citywide graphic.

topInsights.title: LeBron is the season's loudest feeling, and he is on the other bench
topInsights.insight: LeBron James is now a 76er. The Cavs visit for his Philadelphia home debut and face him again in Cup East Group B and the regular season. Cleveland feels 2016 gratitude mixed with 'we are the Cavs now', far stronger than any Knicks grudge. Separately, Nike makes the jersey, so Mitchell and Harden swingmen are Nike sales whatever their shoe deals.
topInsights.implication: Let the schedule set the beat, not the month. Philadelphia's October home opener gets content only. Product waits for the first 76ers night at Rocket Arena: the Group B Cup game if it's in Cleveland, otherwise the first regular-season visit. That may fall in January, and it stays off MLK week. If no home date is confirmed in time, the undated, player-free gratitude tee joins the December gift wave. Mitchell and Harden jerseys sit in the gift plan either way.

topInsights.title: No opener, no Christmas: Black Friday to the MLK noon game
topInsights.insight: Browns Sundays and the Ohio State-Michigan weekend own the fall. With no opening-night or Christmas Day game, the Cavs' first national home stage is the noon Jan 18 rematch with Detroit. Cleveland beat them 125-94 in last spring's Game 7. So the buying season is one arc from Black Friday to MLK weekend, not an October launch.
topInsights.implication: Run one Black Friday-to-MLK arc. The City Edition companion and side line land in late November and early December, Ore Dock layers carry the gift weeks, and Jan 18 is the in-market hero. Never land a drop on a Browns Sunday or the Ohio State-Michigan Saturday.

topInsights.title: Grit is the house style, in ink, stone and steel
topInsights.insight: Music, art and the underground share one graphic language. Think photocopied gig flyers from the Agora, Beachland and Grog Shop, Zygote Press misregistered prints and Julian Stanczak op art. Add the riveted steel of the Hulett ore unloaders and Cuyahoga lift bridges beside the Deco of Terminal Tower and Hope Memorial Bridge. Slick luxury reads as a Portland idea of Cleveland.
topInsights.implication: Winter shells and knits share silhouettes with every cold market. Spend Cleveland's design money only where Chicago, Detroit and Milwaukee can't follow: Hulett truss quilting, ore-dock rust and taconite iron, and stencil type from Flats signage. Add East Side and West Side labels, and Poster Ink credited to named Cleveland rooms and printmakers. Save pristine finishes for performance.

topInsights.title: Parish-and-plate is a goodwill layer, not a headline
topInsights.insight: The Polish Boy (kielbasa crossed with Black East Side barbecue), Stadium Mustard, the West Side Market, paczki day, Lenten fish fries and Dyngus Day are living neighborhood rituals. No other NBA market shares them. But nothing shows fans want food-themed Cavs product at scale.
topInsights.implication: Sell sock and neighborhood-tee micro-runs through partners. Credit the whole Polish Boy lineage (Hot Sauce Williams, Seti's Polish Boys and others) and let the makers choose the lead partner. Keep church imagery off unless a parish asks for it.

topInsights.title: Cleveland celebrates what it watched, not what it was promised
topInsights.insight: 2016 is the shared memory because it came in a Game 7, after decades of The Drive, The Fumble and The Shot. Last spring's two Game 7 wins ended in a Knicks sweep, and a scout has publicly doubted this roster. The deepest untold story is pre-LeBron: Richfield Coliseum and the 1976 'Miracle of Richfield'.
topInsights.implication: Pre-built playoff product prints only the series this team has played, as a gig-flyer tour list from the city that named rock and roll. No title or 'unfinished business' copy. Give Richfield a February heritage night for lifelong diehards, with no help from LeBron.

opportunities.title: Cleveland on the jersey, The Land on the street
opportunities.summary: A City Edition companion line in two layers. Nike 'Cleveland' wordmark fleece and tees, printed on existing blanks, are timed to the City Edition on-sale once its date is announced. A licensed 'The Land' / 216 side collection, made with local apparel brands, gets a named Black Cleveland lead.
where: Ohio City and Gordon Square pop-up
Black-owned Cleveland apparel shops, picked through an open call vetted with Karamu House
CLE Clothing Co. and Ohio Knitting Mills (co-label partners, names and status to confirm)
Lids and Dick's in the suburban mall ring
opportunities.when: The Nike 'Cleveland' layer lands on the City Edition on-sale and first-wear dates once confirmed. The licensed side line launches Saturday Dec 5, a week after Black Friday and clear of the Ohio State-Michigan weekend. A second drop follows on 216 Day (Feb 16) if partners confirm locals mark it. Neither layer waits on the other: if the jersey's on-sale slips past Dec 5, the side line launches alone.
opportunities.how: Source before design. An open call vetted with Karamu House and local Black-owned shops picks the paid lead designer. A named Cleveland hip-hop voice such as Chip tha Ripper (King Chip) is paid and credited as the story partner. Run it as an NBA- and Cavs-licensed collab with Nike or Fanatics manufacturing. Credit the local label on hangtags and agree a set revenue share in writing. Nike makes no claim on 'The Land'.
products: 216 stencil cap in navy and gold
Ohio Knitting Mills collab knit beanie
opportunities.segment: Gen Z and street-level fans plus lifelong diehards who miss the nickname
opportunities.kpi: City Edition and companion sell-through by Dec 31. Collab sell-out time and dollars paid to local partners. Social sentiment on the wordmark change versus the 2025-26 City Edition launch.

opportunities.title: MLK Day capsule co-created with Karamu House
opportunities.summary: A community-led artist series and program for the noon Jan 18 home game against Detroit on NBC. Karamu House and Black Cleveland artists build it around Fairfax, Glenville and East Side history. Only the art is new, printed on existing Nike blanks.
opportunities.when: Pick the artists and finish the artwork by mid-November. Screen-print and embroider on in-stock Nike blanks, release Jan 11-18, 2027, and let the game be the story's peak.
opportunities.how: Lead with Karamu's own story and let its artists set the theme (Carl Stokes-era civic pride, Great Migration neighborhoods). Keep Dr. King's name, likeness and words off product, and clear anything adjacent with the King estate. Publish where the money goes and name every paid artist in the launch copy. If artwork slips past mid-November, run Karamu's community program with a single art tee instead of rushing a series.
products: Artist-series shooting shirt (print on existing blank)
Heavyweight crewneck with embroidered artist mark
opportunities.segment: Black Cleveland families, East Side diehards and the national NBC audience
opportunities.kpi: Funds delivered to Karamu. Artist-series sell-through by Jan 31. MLK weekend arena-store revenue versus a typical January home game.

opportunities.title: Ore Dock: the Hulett layer, Black Friday to MLK
opportunities.summary: Cleveland's share of the league's deep-winter tier. Shared Nike silhouettes get finishes Chicago, Detroit and Milwaukee can't claim: Hulett ore-unloader truss graphics, ore-dock rust and taconite iron, and stencil 'CLEVELAND' from Flats signage. Add an Ohio Knitting Mills knit and East Side or West Side woven labels.
where: Beachwood Place and Legacy Village (East Side label)
Crocker Park and Southpark (West Side label)
Nike Factory Store, Aurora Premium Outlets
opportunities.when: One arc runs from Black Friday, Nov 27, through MLK weekend, Jan 16-18. The hero lands on a weekday Cavs home game in early December. This season is decoration on in-line Therma-FIT and Storm-FIT blanks. The Hulett-quilted shell and waxed-canvas jacket are FW27.
opportunities.how: Sell the Cuyahoga split. The same hoodie and quarter-zip carry an 'East Side' or 'West Side' woven label, allocated by door, so Beachwood and Crocker Park each buy their own bank of the river. Price on a clear entry, swingman and premium ladder for a taxed-apparel market. Fold Mitchell and Harden swingmen into gift bundles. Never launch on a Browns Sunday or the Ohio State-Michigan Saturday.
products: Hulett line-graphic Therma-FIT hoodie in wine (ships now)
East Side / West Side labelled quarter-zip in taconite iron (ships now)
Youth fleece and Mitchell or Harden swingman gift bundle
Hulett-quilted insulated shell in wine and navy (FW27)
opportunities.segment: Suburban families, gift buyers and lifelong diehards on both sides of the river
opportunities.kpi: Q4 fleece and outerwear revenue versus 2025 Q4. East versus West label sell-through by door. Full-price sell-through by Jan 31. Youth bundle units.

opportunities.title: LeBron returns: gratitude, then the Cavs
opportunities.summary: A player-free 'gratitude, then the Cavs' beat for the first 76ers night at Rocket Arena. One side thanks Akron and 2016, the other shows this roster's identity. The October road game at Philadelphia's home opener carries content only.
where: Nike Factory Store, Aurora Premium Outlets
opportunities.when: The schedule sets this, not the month. The Cavs' October road game at Philadelphia's home opener (date to confirm) gets content only. Product goes on the first 76ers game at Rocket Arena: the East Group B Cup meeting (Oct 30-Nov 27) if it's in Cleveland. Otherwise it's the first regular-season visit, which may fall in January and must stay clear of MLK week (Jan 11-18). Fallback: if no home date is confirmed in time for a print run, the undated gratitude tee ships in the December gift wave.
opportunities.how: Clear any Akron, SVSM or 2016 reference with the LeBron James Family Foundation. No LeBron likeness, number or player-led graphics. Copy pairs gratitude with 'we are the Cavs now', and the product is the team, not him.
opportunities.segment: Every segment, especially Akron and lifelong diehards with mixed feelings
opportunities.kpi: Game-night arena-store revenue against a typical home game, the split in social sentiment, and zero complaints from the Foundation or estates

opportunities.title: Rubber City 330 capsule
opportunities.summary: An Akron-only print-and-embellishment capsule: generic tread texture, plain racing stripes and block numerals. It honors Akron's own basketball origin story, with LeBron's SVSM years only as heritage.
where: Nike Factory Store, Aurora Premium Outlets
opportunities.when: Drop in December at Aurora and Summit Mall on existing blanks. Restock with an Akron-creator tee on 330 Day (Mar 30) if locals mark it, otherwise in MAC Tournament week. Reprise in July. A dedicated 330 sneaker colorway is a 2027-28 concept, not this season.
opportunities.how: Co-design with Akron creators, and run any LeBron, SVSM or I Promise reference through the LeBron James Family Foundation. Use no Soap Box Derby name, Derby Downs or Goodyear marks. Stick to generic tread geometry, stripe-and-numeral graphics and a neutral gunmetal.
opportunities.segment: Akron and Summit County fans who identify 330 first
opportunities.kpi: Aurora and Summit Mall sell-through versus a citywide graphic. Akron share of Nike app Cavs sales.

opportunities.title: The Playoff Tour: each series printed like a Cleveland gig flyer
opportunities.summary: A pre-built, quick-turn playoff program in the Poster Ink format. Each round's tee is a flyer for that series, and the back lists every series played, like a tour tee. It records what this team has done instead of promising a title. A Game 7 flyer waits in reserve: the 2016 title came in one, and last spring's run went through two.
where: Nike app and team online shop
Public Square and Warehouse District watch-party sites
opportunities.when: Lock the art in March with a Zygote Press-affiliated printmaker and stage it by the Apr 11 season end. Then it's 48-72 hours from clinch to shelf through each round, peaking in May.
opportunities.how: The artist draws the flyer template and opponent-neutral type in advance. A licensed quick-turn printer adds each opponent and date within 48 hours, and Zygote pulls a small, numbered, hand-printed run per round for the arena store. Copy names Cleveland, the round and the opponent only. Pre-built product carries no 'title', 'unfinished business' or Knicks-revenge lines. If the run ends early, the last tee is still a complete tour record, and unused blanks roll into summer.
products: Round flyer tee (opponent and dates added at clinch)
Tour-back long sleeve listing every series played
Lightweight wine hoodie for April crossover with Guardians crowds
opportunities.segment: Every segment, peaking with casual fans who re-engage in spring
opportunities.kpi: Days from clinch to shelf. Playoff revenue per round versus the 2026 East Finals run. Hand-printed run sell-out time. Out-of-stock rate.

opportunities.title: Richfield '76 heritage line
opportunities.summary: A heritage capsule built on Richfield Coliseum and the 1976 'Miracle of Richfield' (Austin Carr, Jim Chones, Nate Thurmond). Price-era orange-and-blue throwbacks round it out for older collectors.
where: Nike Factory Store, Aurora Premium Outlets
opportunities.when: A February heritage night or Classic Edition game. June 19 gets only a short 2016 gratitude post, with product only if the Cavs are still playing.
opportunities.how: Work with the Cavs and Hardwood Classics licensing, and bring in Austin Carr as storyteller if he's open to it. Keep this the pre-LeBron chapter so it doesn't depend on a 76er. Avoid Juneteenth entirely.
opportunities.segment: Lifelong diehards and Gen X collectors
opportunities.kpi: Sell-through at premium price versus core tees. Share of buyers aged 40+ on the Nike app.

opportunities.title: Neighborhood micro-runs: parish, plate and the Latino West Side
opportunities.summary: Partner-sold micro-runs, not a headline line. A Polish Boy layered-stripe sock and Slavic Village tees cover paczki day, Lent and Dyngus Day. One paid tee-and-cap run with a Clark-Fulton or West 25th Latino artist lands on a spring home game.
where: East Side Polish Boy makers (Hot Sauce Williams, Seti's Polish Boys; lead chosen with them)
Clark-Fulton partner shop via the Julia de Burgos Cultural Arts Center
opportunities.when: From paczki day on Feb 9 through Dyngus Day on Mar 29, 2027. The Latino West Side run goes on a spring home game, since Hispanic Heritage Month ends Oct 15, too soon for product. AsiaTown waits until a partner is identified.
opportunities.how: Credit and pay the whole Black-owned Polish Boy lineage, and let the makers choose who leads. Let the Latino partner pick and pay its artist. Keep church and religious imagery off unless a parish asks. Never copy the Bertman label or make the dish a joke graphic.
products: Latino West Side artist-credited tee and cap
opportunities.segment: West Side and East Side neighborhood loyalists, Puerto Rican and Latino West Side families and Gen Z locals
opportunities.kpi: Partner sell-out time. Earned local media and social mentions. Revenue routed to partner businesses.

collection.name: Said Straight
collection.story: Cleveland just put its own name on the jersey. This collection says the rest just as plainly. Think the ink of its gig posters, the steel of its ore docks and lift bridges, the cold of its lake and the rubber of the 330. Every theme is built with named Cleveland and Akron makers, so it reads as made here, not about here.

themes.name: Poster Ink
themes.story: Photocopied flyers from the Agora, Beachland and Grog Shop, plus Zygote Press misregistration, become the graphic layer beside the 'Cleveland' wordmark. Each print is credited to the room and artist it came from.
themes.segment: Gen Z, creatives and street-level fans
themes.graphics: Stamped, ragged 'CLEVELAND' headline type, halftone and cut-and-paste layouts, intentional offset ink, setlist-style size labels and tour-laminate hangtags.
themes.materials: Garment-dyed heavyweight cotton, plastisol and water-based screen prints with a pre-worn wash, record-sleeve packaging.

pieces.detail: Two-color offset print in wine and gold on newsprint cream, credited printmaker on the neck label.
Back print styled as a home-schedule tour list, with a laminate-style hangtag.
Hand-pulled panel prints with a Zygote Press-affiliated artist, numbered run.
Washed wine six-panel with a photocopy-texture 216 patch.

themes.name: Ore Dock
themes.story: The Hulett ore unloaders that once lined the Cuyahoga, the riveted lift bridges of the Flats and the stepped Deco of Terminal Tower and Hope Memorial Bridge. All cut as heavyweight layers, labelled by the bank of the river the wearer calls home.
themes.segment: Suburban families, gift buyers and premium season-ticket holders
themes.graphics: Hulett unloader silhouette and its truss diagonals as a tonal jacquard and lining print, stepped-setback embossing, gold trim kept small.
themes.materials: Brushed-back heavyweight fleece, waffle and thermal knit, waxed-cotton and duck-canvas panels with rivets and stitched labels, insulated shells.

pieces.detail: Wine in-line Therma-FIT blank with a single-line Hulett unloader and lift-bridge graphic sized for the chest. Ships this season.
Taconite iron in-line blank with an 'East Side' or 'West Side' woven label and a tonal truss-diagonal print on the sleeve. Ships this season.
Wine and gold rib knit made by the Cleveland partner, with a woven civic-type label.
Taconite iron with a wine Hulett-and-bridge line graphic at the hem.
Wine and navy, quilted in the unloader's truss pattern, with a gold zipper pull. FW27 cut-and-sew.
Workwear cut with riveted pockets and a stencil 'CLEVELAND' back hit. FW27 cut-and-sew.

themes.name: Rubber City 330
themes.story: Akron's own chapter: tire-tread texture, racing stripes and block numerals, built with Akron creators as print and embellishment on existing blanks.
themes.graphics: Generic tread-pattern print, plain racing stripes and block numerals, with '330' as the hero mark. No Derby or Goodyear references.
themes.materials: Rubberised tread-texture screen prints, debossed rubber patches and stripe tape applied to existing Nike fleece, tee and warm-up blanks.

pieces.detail: Tread texture across the back yoke, '330' in block numerals.
Racing-stripe tape and block numerals on the thigh, applied to an existing warm-up blank.
Gunmetal crown with a debossed rubber patch.
Wine and gunmetal with a tread-pattern nod on the outsole. A pitch for a later season, not a December 2026 release.

themes.name: The Plate
themes.story: The Polish Boy stack, Stadium Mustard brown and the West Side Market clock tower: the city's immigrant and East Side kitchens as color and pattern.
themes.graphics: Abstract layered stripe in bun tan, fries cream, slaw green and sauce brown. West Side Market tower and arch linework. Lettering inspired by church-hall signs.
themes.materials: Jacquard-knit socks, heavyweight loopback fleece, tonal embroidery.

pieces.detail: Layered-stripe knit. The packaging credits the Polish Boy makers the partners choose.
Clock tower and vaulted-arch drawing, used with the market's input.
Mustard body, wine embroidery, market-hall graphic on the sleeve.

uniform.narrative: A pitch for the 2027-28 City Edition process, since 2026-27 is set. The Hope Memorial Bridge and the Cuyahoga lift bridges carry Cleveland between downtown and the West Side. 'The Crossing' turns that steel and Deco stone into a uniform about one team uniting East Side and West Side, 216 and 330. After a plain-wordmark year, it reaches for Cleveland's own architecture instead of slang or a reissue.

palette.name: Cavs wine
palette.role: base (option B, Association-safe fallback) and trim

motifs: Stepped Deco setbacks abstracted from the bridge pylons and Terminal Tower (geometry only, no carved figures)
Riveted truss diagonals from the Cuyahoga lift bridges and Hulett unloaders
A single Lake Erie horizon line across the hem
uniform.typography: Chest reads 'CLE' in a custom stepped Deco block letter, cut like carved limestone. Navy numbers carry a gold bevel outline. No 'The Land', and no reuse of the Earned 'Cleveland' script.
details: Neck tape reading 'East Side · West Side'
Jock tag with '216 · 330' and a small bridge-span silhouette
Side panels of riveted truss diagonals in rust
Court: a stepped-setback baseline idea for a Cup or arena event, not a uniform deliverable
avoid: The Guardians of Traffic figures, the Guardians name or any Cleveland Guardians mark. Use abstract geometry only.
Another 'The Land' wordmark. The nickname now belongs to the community's own product.
Burning-river flames or 'Mistake on the Lake' jokes that read as outsider mockery
A literal Rock Hall pyramid or other licensed civic logos and the city seal without clearance

partners.name: Karamu House
partners.why: Founded in 1915 and one of the country's oldest Black producing theaters, it's the credible lead for MLK Day and the right vetter for the 'The Land' open call.
partners.idea: Paid co-design of the MLK Day artist series and community program, with proceeds routed to Karamu.

partners.name: Chip tha Ripper (King Chip)
partners.why: A Cleveland hip-hop voice from the music dossier who speaks the city's own vocabulary: a named, credible face for the 'The Land' side line.
partners.idea: Paid, credited story partner for the 'The Land' side line launch, with input on the graphics.

partners.name: Zygote Press

risks.risk: LeBron's first visits as a 76er split the room between gratitude and rivalry, and heritage product can look like promoting an opponent.
risks.mitigation: Keep LeBron to Akron and 2016 history, cleared with the LeBron James Family Foundation. No likeness or player-led graphics, and end the copy on this Cavs team. Confirm the footwear deals of any athlete cast (Harden, Mobley, Watson) before campaigns.

risks.risk: Fans could read the 'Cleveland' wordmark as a step back, and a Nike-run 'The Land' line would look like renting the nickname.
risks.mitigation: Frame the jersey as the city's name worn straight. Run 'The Land' as a licensed collab with a named, paid Black Cleveland lead who keeps credit and a written revenue share.

risks.risk: A title-or-bust team with thin depth and Mitchell's 2027-28 player option could disappoint early, stranding playoff inventory and title messaging.
risks.mitigation: Pre-built playoff product prints only what has happened (the Playoff Tour), with no title or 'unfinished business' copy. Hold blanks, not finished goods, for each round. Keep the winter arc city-led so it sells regardless of results.

risks.risk: Lead times: new cut-and-sew, footwear and a new City Edition cannot land this season.
risks.mitigation: Tag every item 'ships now', 'FW27' or 'uniform cycle'. Every 2026-27 community drop is print or embroidery on in-line Nike blanks. The Hulett-quilted shell, waxed-canvas jacket, The Crossing and the 330 sneaker are FW27 or 2027-28 pitches, with an Association-safe fallback.

risks.risk: Many cues are third-party IP or estate-controlled. They include the Bertman label, Rock Hall, Devo, Bone Thugs, Guardians marks, Goodyear trade dress and the All-American Soap Box Derby. So do the Jesse Owens and King estates, Hardwood Classics and Rockers marks.
risks.mitigation: License or partner before design lock. Use abstract geometry and neutral metallics where rights are unclear. Keep Dr. King's name and words off product, and never reproduce lyrics or logos.

scorecard.rationale: Cleveland has deep, designable local culture: punk and rap lineage, ore-dock steel and Deco civic stone, immigrant food rituals and a distinct Akron identity. Its regional fan base is loyal and title-hungry. The near-term upside is capped, though. Retail is a drive-to-the-mall map with no downtown sneaker district, and the fall wallet is Browns-first. There's only one national home date (MLK Day), and the LeBron storyline is one Nike must handle carefully.
